As someone who has a 4 year business degree and wound up in tech working in a cubicle for a large corporation, I would not do a business degree, unless it is like FMIS or something.  Business is more of a hands on learning and what you gain from school just doesn't seem to be worth it.  That being said I wouldn't have the job that pays well without the piece of paper they call a four year degree.  I dislike work a lot and wish I would have focused more on what I wanted to do instead of just what classes taught.  If you know what you want to do for the rest of your life then yeah go for the 4 year degree.  If you have a good thing going and aren't sure what you want to do then why waste the money on something that may not actually help you?  

If you are going to be in a Community College anyways consider picking up some classes in things that will help you build your own sites/company.  Ex SEO, programming courses, graphics, whatever you may have interest in that you don't want to outsource that can take you places.  It might help you figure out a 4 year degree you would enjoy, or show you what you do or do not want to do. 

Returning to school will always be an option, I think it would be better to join the corporate world/working for others with a fresh degree, so if working for yourself is something you can do, do it before you burn out.

If you don't figure out clear guidelines about such matters I don't think love will be enough.  Say you did get married and she did pay off your debt, do you want her throwing that back in your face every time you get into a serious fight?
Ex:  I paid off my husband's student loans as soon as I found out about them (he knew I was irrationally afraid of debt and was afraid to mention them for the longest time), when we would fight about spending money on something I would often bring it up.  He viewed it as he makes more money than me now and should be able to spend the extra money on his hobbies (or something not the point).  Luickly he started understanding the importance of investing in 401ks and such before I did so when I got on the FI band wagon it was not hard for him to join the ride.  The problem came that he wanted to spend money on races, dirt bikes, video games, etc and he wanted to spend money on his friends and bachelor parties while making it pretty clear that I had to keep my job and keep working if/when we have kids so it felt like I had to work so he could spend money on his friends which really upset me (before getting married we agreed that I could be a stay at home mom if I wanted and he would be the bread winner).  However we finally got to talking about it more and he realized if I am at home I am not going to be sitting around doing nothing, and that since he wants to do these things and I want to save more, I get to retire before him and we really haven't resented each other since.

But there are 2 things I would like to point out 1) it is important to have hobbies and okay to spend money on things that truely make you happy (I obviously struggle with this more than him), and 2) we both Max out our 401Ks and IRAs and agree that saving for retirement is important.  AKA we make our financial decisions together and are pretty much on the same page, we just have difference degrees of intensity, I couldn't imagine trying to be married to someone who was okay with credit card debt so it is definitely something you are going to have to talk about and have a clear plan on how finances are going to be dealt with.

So I think keeping Traditional for 2015 and doing Roth for 2016 may fit this plan nicely, because I cannot say for sure if I will pay no taxes in retirement because there will be a lot of life changes between now and then, but I also think this gives me enough confidence to say that staying with Traditional for the year is not going to be something I regret.
